classification.difficultyReason: Count the incident edges at each marked vertex and identify the even degrees.

content.prompt: How many vertices of even degree does this network have?

spec.description: Seven unlabelled vertices, preserving the straight paths through the marked central and interior vertices. Ordinary source-blue edges and markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Internal positional identifiers only: edges AB, AD, AC, BC, CE, CF, CG, DE, DF, EF and FG. Degrees are A=3, B=2, C=5, D=3, E=3, F=4 and G=2. Identifiers are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertices and edges are permanent givens; no answer markings are shown.

answer.worked: The top-right vertex of the rectangular section and the far-right vertex each have degree 2. The bottom-right vertex of the rectangular section has degree 4. The other vertices have degrees 3, 3, 3 and 5. Therefore, 3 vertices have even degree.
